_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce the risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, event-driven trial of finerenone added to standard of care with stable ACEi or ARB
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a clinical diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease (CKD associated with T2DM)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: time to first occurrence of the composite of onset of kidney failure, sustained decrease of eGFR ≥40% from baseline over at least 4 weeks, or renal death. Key secondary: time to first occurrence of CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite met: 504 (17.8%) finerenone vs 600 (21.1%) placebo, HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.73, 0.93), p=0.001. Key secondary CV composite: HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.75, 0.99), p=0.034.

key_safety: Most frequently reported (≥10%) adverse reaction was hyperkalemia (18.3% finerenone vs 9.0% placebo). Other adverse reactions more common than placebo: hypotension (4.8% vs 3.4%) and hyponatremia (1.4% vs 0.7%). Hyperkalemia led to permanent discontinuation in 2.3% vs 0.9% and hospitalization in 1.4% vs 0.3%.
target_moa: Finerenone is a nonsteroidal, selective antagonist of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), which is activated by aldosterone and cortisol; it blocks MR-mediated sodium reabsorption and MR overactivation in epithelial (kidney) and nonepithelial (heart, blood vessels) tissues, reducing fibrosis and inflammation.

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population.

description.text: Added FIGARO-DKD cardiovascular outcomes data in patients with type 2 diabetes and diabetic kidney disease to the label

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of the results of the FIGARO-DKD study (Study 17530) entitled, "A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, event driven Phase III study to investigate the efficacy and safety of finerenone on the reduction of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus and the clinical diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease in addition to standard of care," into the currently approved label.

description.text: Added indication to reduce risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent heart failure visits in adults with heart failure with LVEF ≥40%

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for a new indication to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent heart failure visits in adult patients with heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \ge 40\%.

summary.text: NDA 215341 for finerenone (Kerendia) was submitted by Bayer HealthCare on November 6, 2020 (received November 9, 2020), reviewed under Priority review with a PDUFA goal date of 7/9/2021 and approved on that date (first cycle). The program held Fast-Track designation granted February 4, 2015. It was a full (traditional) approval, not accelerated, based on the single Phase 3 FIDELIO-DKD trial.
